types.feature_dump: Feature dump instead of digging into their problem
types.argued: Argued with the buyer or brushed off what they said
types.discount: Discounted without a reason (caved on price)
types.no_next_step: Ended without a specific next step
types.trash_competitor: Trashed the competitor or the last vendor
types.ignored_pain: Skipped right past a pain they just shared
types.pitch_early: Pitched a solution before finishing discovery
types.talked_past: Dodged or talked past the objection
types.no_intro: Didn't say who they are or why they're there
types.overpromise: Overpromised something they can't back up

calls.title: The Busy Dental Office
calls.buyer: Marisol, office manager at Bright Smiles Dental
lines: Hi Marisol, this is Jordan with BookWell. I'm calling because we help dental offices cut down on no-shows. Did I catch you at an okay time?
I've got like two minutes. There's a patient at the desk.
I'll be quick. How are you handling appointment reminders right now?
Our front desk calls everyone the day before. It's a lot, honestly.
Got it. So BookWell does automatic texts, emails, two-way confirmations, waitlist fill, online booking, insurance verification, and it plugs right into Dentrix.
Okay... that's a lot of stuff. We already use the reminders in Dentrix.
Right, but the Dentrix reminders are pretty basic. Most offices find they don't really work.
Well, they work fine for us.
Fair enough. When a patient no-shows, what happens to that chair for the hour?
It just sits there. Dr. Patel hates it. We had four last Tuesday.
Four in one day. What does one empty hour cost you, roughly?
I don't know, a cleaning is like 180 bucks. More for crowns.
So that Tuesday alone was around seven hundred dollars walking out the door.
Yeah. Okay. But I really can't take on another system right now.
Totally understand. I can do 30 percent off the first year if you sign up this month.
It's not really about the money, it's the setup. We're short-staffed.
Makes sense. Setup is on us, it takes about an hour of your time total. Would it help to walk Dr. Patel through it together?
Maybe. Just send me some info and I'll show him.
Sounds good, I'll email you something today!

5.why: She just said reminder calls are "a lot." That's a pain worth digging into. Instead the rep listed seven features.
5.fix: "A lot how? Roughly how many hours a week does the front desk spend on those calls?"

7.why: Telling her the tool she chose "doesn't really work" makes her defend it. And she did.
7.fix: "Makes sense. How's that been working with no-shows?"

15.why: Her objection was workload, not price. The discount answered a question she never asked and made the price look fake.
15.fix: "When you say another system, what worries you most, the setup or training the team?"

19.why: "Send me info" is where deals go to die. Nothing is on the calendar, and Dr. Patel, the decision maker, isn't involved.
19.fix: "Happy to. Would 15 minutes with you and Dr. Patel on Thursday at lunch be easier than an email he might not read?"

calls.title: The Expired Listing
calls.buyer: Greg, homeowner whose listing expired this morning
lines: Hi, is this Greg? This is Taylor Brooks with Coastline Realty. I saw your home on Maple came off the market this morning.
Yeah, and you're the ninth agent to call me today. What do you want?
I bet. I'm calling for the same reason they are, I won't pretend otherwise. Can I ask you one question before you hang up on me?
Why do you think it didn't sell?
Honestly? The price. My agent told me 950 and we got two showings in three months.
Your agent really dropped the ball. Nine-fifty was never realistic for that street.
Well, I'm the one who pushed for that number, so...
Understood. Where are you and your family hoping to be six months from now?
We're supposed to move to Phoenix. My new job starts in April.
Okay. And what have you been doing to keep the house show-ready?
I mean, we cleaned it. I don't know.
Here's what I'd do differently: pro photos, a video walkthrough, and price it at 899 to start a bidding war.
899? You haven't even seen the inside. The kitchen is brand new.
You're right, I haven't. That's exactly why I'd want to walk it with you. What does your wife think about relisting?
She wants to just rent it out and deal with it later.
Renting is a real option. Would you both be open to 20 minutes Thursday at 6, so I can show you renting versus selling side by side?
...Thursday could work. Let me check with her.
Perfect. Want to loop her in right now, or should I text you both a confirmation after you talk tonight?

7.why: Bashing the last agent backfired. Greg picked that price, so the rep just insulted Greg.
7.fix: "That's tough. What did you and your agent base the 950 on?"

11.why: Greg just revealed a hard deadline: a job starting in April. That's the reason to act, and the rep skipped right past it.
11.fix: "April. So what happens if the house isn't sold by then?"

13.why: Naming a price before seeing the house or finishing discovery. Greg called it out immediately.
13.fix: "I'd want to see it before I say anything about price. What do you think buyers didn't love when they walked through?"

calls.title: The New Mom Quote Request
calls.buyer: Kim, on maternity leave, requested a quote online
lines: Hi Kim, it's Andre from Shieldline. You requested a life insurance quote online on Monday. Is now still an okay time?
Sure, the baby's napping, so I have like ten minutes.
Perfect. And congrats on the baby! What got you looking at coverage now?
My husband keeps saying we need it. We just bought a house and I'm on maternity leave.
Makes sense. How much coverage were you thinking?
I have no idea. Like 250? My work gives me some already.
You'll definitely want at least a million. Most families need ten times their income.
A million? That sounds really expensive.
It's actually super affordable, trust me. It's less than a coffee a day.
I mean, money is tight with me on leave.
Totally fair. Can I ask, what would your husband need to cover if something happened to you?
The mortgage, I guess. And daycare. That's like two grand a month alone.
So the mortgage, plus daycare for the next five years or so.
Yeah. When you put it that way...
If we covered the mortgage and daycare for around thirty-five a month, would that feel doable?
Maybe. I need to talk to my husband first.
Of course. Just so you know, this rate is only guaranteed until Friday.
Oh. Okay... I'll let you know.

7.why: The rep picked a number without asking about income, the mortgage, or what her work covers. It scared her off.
7.fix: "Let's figure out the right number together. What would your family need to cover if you weren't here?"

9.why: "Trust me" and a cliché brushed off a real budget worry. She repeated it because she didn't feel heard.
9.fix: "That's fair, especially on leave. What monthly number would feel comfortable?"

17.why: Fake urgency right after she asked to talk to her husband. It kills the trust the rep just built.
17.fix: "Of course, he should be part of this. Want to do a quick call with both of you tomorrow night?"

19.why: "I'll let you know" plus "talk soon" means this deal probably dies. No time, no plan, no husband on the call.
19.fix: "What time tomorrow works for a 10-minute call with both of you? I'll bring two options."

calls.title: The Price-Shopper Phone-Up
calls.buyer: Alicia, calling about a used RAV4 on the website
lines: Thanks for calling Harbor Toyota, this is Mike. How can I help?
Hi, I'm calling about the 2021 RAV4 on your website. Is it still available?
It is. That's a nice one: 32,000 miles, one owner, clean Carfax.
Okay. What's your best price? The site says 28,9.
I can probably get my manager to do 27,500 for you.
Hm. Another dealer has one for 26,800.
What's got you shopping for an SUV right now?
I've got twins on the way, and my Civic isn't going to cut it.
Congrats! Do you want to come in today at 4 or tomorrow at 10?
Slow down, I'm just trying to get a price.
Totally fair. Besides price, what matters most to you in the next car?
Honestly, safety. And fitting two car seats in the back without it being a nightmare.
That's a great thing to check on the 26,800 one too. Did they mention whether it has the safety package?
Ours has it. And I can have two car seats installed so you can see exactly how they fit. You could bring yours if you already have them.
Awesome, so you're definitely buying it if the car seats fit, right?
Fair enough. How's Saturday at 11? I'll have both seats in and the car pulled up front.

4.why: The rep dropped $1,400 before learning anything about her. Now she knows the price is soft and anchors even lower.
4.fix: "I'll get you a great number. Before I do, what are you comparing it to?"

8.why: Twins on the way is a huge reason to buy: safety, space, car seats. The rep jumped straight to an appointment close.
8.fix: "Twins, congrats! What's most important in the car with two babies coming?"

16.why: A leading yes/no "trap" question right after she warmed up. It made her back off.
16.fix: "If the seats fit the way you want, what else would you need to feel good about it?"

calls.title: The Door Knock
calls.buyer: Linda, homeowner, bill is about $400 in summer
lines: Sorry! I'm Chris with SunPeak. We're doing free energy reviews for houses on your street this week.
We're not interested in solar. We looked into it.
Totally fair. What made you decide against it?
The guy wanted 40 grand and said our bill would be zero. I didn't buy it.
Yeah, a lot of companies overpromise. We're honestly the only ones who don't.
You're right, they do. What's your electric bill running in summer?
Like four hundred. The AC runs all day because my mom lives with us and the heat's hard on her.
Four hundred is high. With solar you could save up to 80 percent.
Fair. What would have to be true for this to even be worth looking at again?
No money down, and it can't be a 25-year loan like my neighbor's.
We have zero down, and there are options without a 25-year term. Would it be crazy to look at real numbers from your actual bill?
Maybe. My husband handles this stuff.
When's he home? I can come back tonight and we'll do it in 20 minutes.
Great. And if the numbers work, you'd sign tonight, right?

1.why: Asking a qualifying question before saying who you are. At a door, that's instantly suspicious.
1.fix: "Hi, I'm Chris with SunPeak. We're doing quick energy reviews on your street. Are you the homeowner?"

7.why: "We're the only ones who don't overpromise" is itself an overpromise, and it knocks the competition. She saw right through it.
7.fix: "That's frustrating. What would you have wanted him to be straight with you about?"

11.why: Her mom's health is why the AC runs all day. That's the emotional reason, and the rep went straight to a stat.
11.fix: "That makes sense with your mom. Does the bill ever make you think twice about running it?"

19.why: Asking for a commitment to sign before the husband has seen a single number. She'll likely cancel the 6pm visit.
19.fix: "Great, 6:15 it is. I'll bring the numbers from your bill and you two can decide if it makes sense."

calls.title: The IT Director
calls.buyer: Tom, IT director at a manufacturing company
lines: Hi Tom, Priya with Sentra. We help manufacturers stop phishing before it reaches the inbox. Do you have 30 seconds?
Are you happy with your current email security?
Yep. We're good. We use Microsoft Defender.
Makes sense, a lot of teams do. When something does slip past Defender, what does cleanup look like for your team?
Last month someone in accounting wired 60 grand to a fake vendor. That was a fun week.
Oof. Sixty thousand. Were you able to recover any of it?
About half. The CFO is still on my case about it.
Sentra uses AI behavioral analysis and a proprietary threat graph, so it's basically impossible for that to happen again.
Nothing's impossible. What happens when it flags a real invoice?
"Basically never" isn't an answer. My AP team can't have invoices stuck.
You're right, that's a real concern. Flagged emails go to a queue your team releases in one click, and you can allow-list vendors. Do you know your false-positive rate with Defender today?
Would it help to run Sentra silently next to Defender for two weeks, so you can see what it would have caught and what it would have flagged by mistake?
Maybe. I'd have to get the CFO on board. It's his budget.
Makes sense. What would he need to see to say yes?
Probably that it would have stopped the wire fraud.
Perfect, I'll send you a case study on that.

3.why: "Are you happy?" hands him an easy "yep" and a way off the call.
3.fix: "How are you handling phishing today, and what's slipped through lately?"

9.why: Buzzwords plus "basically impossible." A technical buyer immediately stops trusting you.
9.fix: "That's exactly the attack we're built for. Can I ask how that email got past Defender?"

11.why: He raised a real technical objection and the rep dodged it with a hand-wave.
11.fix: "Good question. Here's exactly what happens when a real invoice gets flagged..."

19.why: The CFO is the decision maker and his criteria were just handed over. A case study by email wastes that.
19.fix: "Could we get 20 minutes with you and the CFO next week? I'll show how it would have caught that exact wire."

calls.title: The Warehouse Manager
calls.buyer: Ray, operations manager at a distribution center
lines: Ray, Dana from ShiftForce. We staff warehouses in the Inland Empire. Did I catch you in the middle of something?
I'm always in the middle of something. What do you need?
I noticed you're hiring 15 pickers on Indeed. How's that going?
It's not. People show up for two days and quit.
Two days. What do you think is driving that?
The work is hard, and the Amazon down the street pays a dollar more.
We can match Amazon's pay easily, that's no problem.
Then your markup must be crazy. What do you charge?
Our bill rate is 1.6 times the pay rate.
1.6? The last agency did 1.4, and I still dumped them.
Why were you at 1.6 a second ago?
Fair question. What made you dump the last agency?
Half their people didn't show, and nobody answered the phone at 5 a.m. when I needed replacements.
So the real cost wasn't the rate. It was the no-shows and the dead phone line.
We keep backup workers on call for day one, and our on-call line answers at 5 a.m. Want to try it with five pickers next week?
A trial I could do. What's it going to cost me?
Let's not worry about price right now. The important thing is getting you people.

7.why: Promising to match Amazon's pay without knowing the margins. Ray immediately figured the markup must be huge.
7.fix: "Pay's part of it. When people quit after two days, what do they tell you?"

11.why: The rate dropped the moment he pushed back. Now he knows it's negotiable and trusts the 1.6 less.
11.fix: "Fair. What made the 1.4 agency not worth it?"

19.why: He asked a direct price question and the rep dodged it. Dodging price feels shady right when he's ready to say yes.
19.fix: "For a five-person trial at 1.5, it's about $X a week. If they stick, we talk volume."

calls.title: The Renewal That's Slipping
calls.buyer: Sarah, marketing director, renewal on the 30th
lines: Hey Sarah, it's Ben from Pulse. Your renewal is coming up on the 30th, so I wanted to check in.
Yeah, good timing actually. We're planning to cancel.
Oh, I'm glad you told me. Can I ask why?
We're barely using it. Maybe two people log in. And it's eighteen grand a year.
I can take 20 percent off if you renew today.
It's not really about the price. Nobody uses it.
Why do you think the team stopped using it?
The person who set it up left in March. Nobody really knows how it works now.
That's on us. We should have caught that when she left.
Well, it's honestly really easy to use. Most people learn it in a day.
Then why is nobody using it?
Fair. What were you hoping Pulse would do for the team when you bought it?
Weekly reports for leadership, without someone spending all Friday in spreadsheets.
And who's building those reports now?
Do you want to renew so we can fix that?
What if I set up your Friday report myself this week and train two people on a 30-minute call Tuesday? If it doesn't save your Fridays by the 30th, you cancel, no hard feelings.

5.why: Throwing a discount at a usage problem. The problem was that nobody uses it, not the price.
5.fix: "That's fair. Who are the two people still using it, and what for?"

11.why: Right after owning the problem, the rep undercut it by telling her it's easy. That implies her team is the problem.
11.fix: "What would it take for the team to actually rely on it again?"

17.why: A yes/no renewal ask before offering any plan to fix it. Easy "no."
17.fix: Propose the fix first, then ask: "If I set up your Friday report this week, would that change things?"
